_description: Material technique: Fresnel (rim lighting, edge glow, shield effects). Essential for magic auras, shields, hologram edges, character highlights.
overview: Fresnel effect makes surfaces brighter at glancing angles (edges) and darker at direct-facing angles (center). In UE5, the Fresnel node outputs 0 at surface center, 1 at edges.

material_setup.blend_mode: Translucent or Additive (most common for VFX)
material_setup.shading_model: Unlit (for pure emissive VFX) or Default Lit

FresnelExponent.note: Higher = thinner edge, Lower = wider glow. 2-4 is sweet spot for most VFX.

custom_fresnel_manual.description: Build fresnel manually for more control (recommended for advanced VFX)

steps.nodes: Dot(VertexNormalWS, CameraDirectionWS) → result is 1 at center, 0 at edges
1 - DotResult → Power(x, Exponent) → gives you 0 at center, 1 at edges with controllable falloff

custom_fresnel_manual.advantage: Can manipulate the dot product (offset, remap) for unique looks

shield_bubble.extra: Add panning hex pattern texture multiplied with fresnel for tech shield look

character_aura.extra: Animate intensity with sine wave for pulse effect

hologram.extra: Add scanlines (WorldPosition.Z * frequency → frac → step) multiplied with fresnel

ghost_character.extra: Distortion on center to see through, solid at edges

hit_flash.note: Applied as overlay to character material on hit

fresnel_with_noise.description: Break up the clean fresnel edge with noise for organic look
fresnel_with_noise.method: Multiply fresnel result with noise texture before applying color. Creates flickering, unstable edge.

dual_fresnel.description: Two fresnel layers at different exponents for inner/outer glow

animated_fresnel.description: Pulse, breathe, or flicker the fresnel edge
animated_fresnel.method: Multiply intensity by: Sine(Time * Speed) * 0.5 + 0.5 for pulse, or noise for flicker

world_position_mask.description: Fresnel only on certain parts of mesh (e.g., top half only)
world_position_mask.method: Lerp(0, FresnelResult, WorldPositionMask) where mask is based on Z height or custom vertex color

common_mistakes: Exponent too high (>6) → edge almost invisible, wasted effect
Exponent too low (<1.5) → entire surface glows, loses rim-light quality
Not using emissive → fresnel without glow looks flat and unimpressive
Applying to opaque material → you see the color but not the rim-light shape, must use translucent/additive
Forgetting to disable depth test for inner surfaces → z-fighting artifacts
